title: Graph isomorphisms and incidence matrices
section: Graph Theory ▷ Graph Isomorphism; Review Matrices
terms: graph isomorphism; adjacency preservation; adjacency matrix; incidence matrix; unori- ented incidence matrix; graph invariant.

exposition.text:
A graph isomorphism is a vertex bijection preserving adjacency in both directions. The draw-
ing’s shape and line crossings are irrelevant unless a crossing is designated as a vertex. Vertex
count, edge count, degree multiset, connectedness, and cycle counts are invariants, although
agreeing on a few invariants does not prove isomorphism.
For a simple graph, the adjacency matrix has entry 1 when two vertices are adjacent and 0
otherwise. The unoriented incidence matrix has rows for vertices and columns for edges, with
1 at the two endpoints of each edge. Each column sums to two, row sums are degrees, and

Let B be the unoriented incidence matrix of a simple graph. If tr(BB ) = 26, how many edges
does the graph have?
(A) 6 (B) 13 (C) 26 (D) 39 (E) 52

solution.text:
T
The diagonal of BB contains the vertex degrees. Their sum is twice the number of edges,
so 2m = 26 and m = 13.

question.text:
Which invariant proves that a cycle on six vertices is not isomorphic to the disjoint union of
two triangles?
(A) Number of vertices
(B) Number of edges
(C) Degree sequence
(D) Number of connected components
(E) Number of vertices of odd degree

solution.text:
Both graphs have six vertices, six edges, all degrees two, and no odd-degree vertices. The
six-cycle is connected, whereas the two triangles form two connected components.

question.text:
3
For the adjacency matrix A of a simple graph, tr(A ) = 42. How many triangles does the graph
contain?
(A) 6 (B) 7 (C) 14 (D) 21 (E) 42

solution.text:
3
The diagonal entries of A count closed walks of length three. Every triangle contributes
three starting vertices and two directions, hence six walks. Divide 42 by six to obtain seven
triangles.
